newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: W. Australia miners say probing gold royalty move.
newsitem.headline: W. Australia miners say probing gold royalty move.

text.p: The Perth-based Association of Mining and Exploration Companies Inc (AMEC) has stiffened its opposition to the Western Australian (WA) royalty on gold production, accusing the state government of misconduct in its use of state treasury.
AMEC said in a statement on Wednesday it had made an application under the Freedom of Information Act to probe how the government arrived at its recent decision to implement a gold royalty.
"The association wants to know if State Treasury made a secret report to the government headed 'Revenue Threats and Opportunities' before a decision was made," the statement said.

"We understand that this report went far outside the role and responsibility of a government Treasury and apparently concentrated on a tactical and political role rather than that of a senior financial adviser to the government," said George Savell, AEMC executive director.

"It appears that a special Treasury project team put forward a list of threats to the tax, listing AMEC high on the list, and suggested strategies on how to neutralise opposition and gain acceptance to the tax both from the general public and the industry itself," he said.
AMEC accuses the government of using its agencies, including the Department of Minerals and Energy, to gather intelligence on the industry's stance.
This was unacceptable and outside a government department's traditional role, Savell said.
The Western Australian government earlier this month announced it would impose a royalty on gold production at an initial rate of 1.25 percent, increasing to 2.5 percent in 1999/2000.

Western Australia is Australia's main gold state, producing about 180 tonnes a year from the national total of 240 tonnes-250 tonnes. AMEC has said that a 2.5 percent royalty would cost state gold miners more than A$500 million in lost production and at least A$200 million in lost investments.
AMEC represents 230 Australian mining, exploration and services companies and individuals.
